title: Getting Around Nakhon Ratchasima (Korat) — Bus, Train, Songthaew, Taxi/Grab vs Car Rental | ThailandAddict
metaDesc: Compare ways to get to Nakhon Ratchasima (Korat) and get around the province — bus/van from Bangkok, the Isan rail line, in-town songthaews and tuk-tuks, metered taxis/Grab, and renting a car for Phimai and Dan Khun Thot, with real approximate prices, pros and cons, and what to know before choosing.
ogTitle: Getting Around Nakhon Ratchasima (Korat) — Bus, Train, Songthaew, Taxi/Grab vs Car Rental
ogDesc: Coming to Korat from Bangkok, take a bus or van for about 3-4 hours, or ride the Isan rail line. In town there are songthaews, tuk-tuks, and Grab, while farther-flung Phimai and Dan Khun Thot call for a rental car or songthaew — a guide to choosing by budget and travel style, updated 2026
intro: Nakhon Ratchasima (Korat) is a gateway to Isan that's easy to reach from Bangkok in several ways. You can take a bus or van for about 3-4 hours along the motorway, or ride the Isan rail line straight into Nakhon Ratchasima station. Flights are very limited, so they're not really a mainstream option. Once you're in town, there are songthaews, tuk-tuks, metered taxis, and Grab to get around. But standout sights like Phimai Historical Park sit about 60 kilometers outside the city, and Dan Khun Thot is even farther, so many travelers end up weighing convenience, cost, and freedom against each other. This page compares every option for both arriving in the province and getting around once you're there, with real approximate prices and the caveats for each.

blocks.html:
Korat is a large province with attractions spread far apart — from the city center with the Thao Suranari Monument (locally called Ya Mo), night markets, and big malls, to Phimai Historical Park about 60 kilometers outside town, and the nature spots around Dan Khun Thot and Wang Nam Khiao even farther out. So planning your trip really splits into two questions: how do you get to Korat, and how do you get around once you're there — because these two use completely different transport and budgets.

Worth knowing upfront: getting to Korat is easy by bus or van from Mo Chit, or by the Isan rail line. Nakhon Ratchasima airport has very few flights, so it isn't the main option for most travelers. Once you're in the city, songthaews and tuk-tuks still cover short trips cheaply, while Grab and metered taxis are more convenient when you're carrying bags or heading back late. But if you're going to Phimai or other far-flung spots, renting a car is usually the best value and most freedom. Below is an overview comparison first, followed by details on each option.

blocks.name: Bus / Van, Bangkok-Korat
blocks.area: Mo Chit 2 (Bangkok) → Nakhon Ratchasima bus terminal
blocks.bestFor: Most travelers coming from Bangkok who want to save money and skip driving
blocks.priceRange: Budget · roughly a few hundred baht per trip (bus/van, varies by company and seat class)

gallery.alt: A public van of the type that runs between provinces in Thailand (illustrative)
Mittraphap Road, the main route into Korat (illustrative)

blocks.descHtml:
For most travelers coming to Korat from Bangkok, the bus and van are the cheapest and most convenient options. Departures leave Mo Chit 2 bus terminal frequently throughout the day, running the motorway and Mittraphap Road straight into Korat, taking around 3-4 hours depending on traffic. Fares run a few hundred baht per trip, with a choice between spacious air-conditioned coaches and more frequent vans. You'll arrive at Nakhon Ratchasima bus terminal, which sits within the city, so you can hop straight onto a songthaew, tuk-tuk, or Grab to your hotel.

One thing to prepare for: some vans can be fairly cramped with limited legroom. If you're tall or carrying a lot of luggage, the coach bus will be more comfortable. Tickets sell out fast over long holidays or festivals, so book ahead or arrive at the station with time to spare, and check whether your route ends at the new bus terminal or an in-town stop, since different companies use different drop-off points. If you're traveling at night, plan your onward transport into town in advance too, since songthaews thin out a lot after dark.
blocks.tipHtml: Tip: If you don't like cramped vans, choose a premium air-conditioned coach instead — it's only a small price difference and far more comfortable. Over long holidays, book your ticket in advance, since the popular morning and evening departures fill up fast.
pros: The cheapest option compared to renting a car or flying
Frequent departures all day from Mo Chit 2, no long waits
Fast, around 3-4 hrs via the motorway and Mittraphap Road
Arrives at the in-town bus terminal, easy onward transport to your hotel
cons: Some vans are cramped with limited legroom
Tickets sell out fast over long holidays and festivals — book ahead
Arriving at night can make onward transport to your hotel harder to find than during the day

blocks.name: Isan rail line (to Nakhon Ratchasima station)
blocks.area: Bangkok (Bang Sue Central/Hua Lamphong) → Nakhon Ratchasima station
blocks.bestFor: Travelers who enjoy the train experience, unhurried trips, want to see the scenery along the way
blocks.duration: Longer than road transport (depends on class and train)
blocks.priceRange: Cheap to moderate · depends on seat class and train type
blocks.alt: A train at Nakhon Ratchasima station (illustrative)

gallery.alt: A train stopped at Nakhon Ratchasima station (illustrative)

blocks.descHtml:
The Isan rail line is another classic way to reach Korat. Trains run from Bangkok (Krung Thep Aphiwat Central Terminal/Bang Sue, with some services still passing through Hua Lamphong), heading up into Isan and arriving at Nakhon Ratchasima station, which sits right in the city, making onward transport to your hotel easy. There are several classes and train types to choose from, from budget rapid trains to more comfortable services. The appeal of the train is the scenery along the way as you climb onto the Isan plateau — an experience a bus simply can't match. It suits travelers who aren't in a rush and want a slower-paced way to travel.

What to understand: trains generally take longer than buses, and some services can run late depending on conditions. So it's not ideal if you're pressed for time or have a fixed onward connection. Check the timetable and book your seat in advance, especially over long holidays, since the better classes sell out fast. If traveling at night, pick a service that arrives in Korat at a time when onward transport is still easy to find, and always build in some buffer time so your first day's plans aren't too rushed.
blocks.tipHtml: Tip: Check the schedule and book tickets in advance through the State Railway's channels, especially over long holidays, and choose a train that arrives in Korat during the day or early evening — it's much easier to find onward transport than on a late-night arrival.
pros: Arrives at an in-town station, easy onward transport to your hotel
Scenic ride, with views as you climb onto the Isan plateau
Multiple classes and services to choose from depending on budget
Great for travelers who aren't in a rush and want an easygoing trip
cons: Takes noticeably longer than the bus or van
Some trains can run late — not ideal if you're in a hurry or have a fixed schedule
Better-class tickets sell out fast over long holidays — book ahead

blocks.name: Songthaew / tuk-tuk in town
blocks.bestFor: Budget travelers making short trips around town in the daytime, no rush
blocks.duration: Runs fixed routes, mostly during the day
blocks.priceRange: Cheapest option · songthaews run tens of baht per person · tuk-tuks require negotiation

gallery.alt: A street in central Nakhon Ratchasima (illustrative)

blocks.descHtml:
Within Korat city, the songthaew is the cheapest way to get around. These run fixed routes linking key areas — the Thao Suranari Monument, markets, malls, and the bus terminal — with fares running just tens of baht per person on the main routes. Simply flag one down along its route and press the buzzer or tell the driver when you want to get off. It suits budget travelers making short in-town trips who aren't in a rush, giving you a slice of local atmosphere an app-hailed ride can't offer. Tuk-tuks (the Korat-style three-wheelers) are also available to hail, better suited for short hops that songthaews don't cover.

The catch to know: songthaews run limited routes and hours, mostly operating from daytime into early evening, thinning out — or disappearing entirely — late at night, and they don't reach every side street or destination. If your hotel is off the main route, you may need to walk the rest of the way or call a Grab instead. Tuk-tuks have no meter, so you must agree on the fare before boarding every time, and clarify whether it's per person or for the whole ride. Overall, songthaews and tuk-tuks are great value for daytime in-town trips along their routes, but not ideal for nighttime travel or trips outside the city.
blocks.tipHtml: Tip: Ask your hotel or locals which songthaew route passes your destination and how late it runs, since they're hard to find after dark. And when taking a tuk-tuk, always agree on the fare before boarding, and clarify clearly whether it's per person or for the whole vehicle.
pros: The cheapest way to get around town, songthaews run just tens of baht per person
Hop on along the route, no booking or app needed
Connects key areas — Ya Mo, markets, malls, and the bus terminal
Gives you a real taste of local atmosphere along the way
cons: Limited routes, doesn't reach every side street — hotels off-route mean extra walking
Mostly runs during the day, thinning out a lot or stopping entirely after dark
Tuk-tuks have no meter — you must negotiate the fare before every ride

blocks.name: Metered taxi / Grab
blocks.area: In town, bus terminal, train station, airport
blocks.bestFor: Carrying heavy luggage, returning late at night, or heading somewhere songthaews don't reach and you don't want to wait
blocks.priceRange: Moderate · Grab shows the price before you book · taxis run the meter
blocks.alt: Grab app-hailed vehicles in a Thai city (illustrative)

gallery.alt: The atmosphere of Nakhon Ratchasima city (illustrative)

blocks.descHtml:
When you're carrying heavy luggage, heading back late, or going somewhere songthaews don't reach, Grab and metered taxis are the most convenient option in Korat. Grab works reliably within the city and picks up and drops off at the bus terminal, train station, and major hotel areas. The advantage is seeing the price before you book, so there's no need to haggle, and you can pay by cash or card. Metered taxis also operate in town and can be hailed at major spots, useful when Grab is hard to find. Having both options gives you a lot more flexibility getting around the city, especially once the songthaews have stopped running for the day.

The limitation to understand: the number of Grab cars in Korat isn't as high as in a big city like Bangkok. Late at night or when heading somewhere outside town, you may wait longer or struggle to find a ride, and prices surge automatically during rush hour or rain. Taxis in the provinces are also fewer than in the capital, and sometimes you'll need to call ahead. If you're planning to go all the way to Phimai or another far-flung spot, hailing an app ride one-way will be expensive and finding a return ride difficult — in that case, renting a car or hiring a driver for the day is usually better value. Grab and taxis are best suited for in-town and mid-range trips rather than a full day exploring outside the city.
blocks.tipHtml: Tip: Open the Grab app to check if cars are available in your area before planning a late return — if supply is low, build in extra time or ask your hotel to help call a local taxi. And if you're heading far outside the city for the whole day, compare the price of hiring a car for the day against booking app rides one-way — hiring usually works out cheaper.
pros: Grab shows the price before you book — no need to negotiate
Convenient when carrying heavy bags or returning late after songthaews stop
Reaches all over the city and spots songthaews don't cover
Both Grab and metered taxis available as backups for each other
cons: Fewer Grab cars than in Bangkok — may mean longer waits late at night
Grab prices surge automatically during rush hour and rain
Not worth it for a full day out of town — hiring a car or driver is better value

blocks.name: Car rental (for Phimai-Dan Khun Thot-Wang Nam Khiao)
blocks.area: Pick up in town → Phimai ~60 km / Dan Khun Thot / Wang Nam Khiao
blocks.bestFor: Travelers visiting multiple spots outside the city, wanting freedom without waiting for transport, groups or families
blocks.priceRange: ฿900-1,500/day (small car to family car), not including fuel or full insurance
blocks.alt: A car rental sign in Thailand (illustrative)

gallery.alt: A small car of the type commonly rented in Thailand (illustrative)
Phimai Historical Park, a standout attraction outside Korat city (illustrative)

blocks.descHtml:
Many of Korat's standout attractions sit outside the city, especially Phimai Historical Park, about 60 kilometers from town, as well as the nature spots around Dan Khun Thot and Wang Nam Khiao. Renting a car is usually the best value and most freedom for travelers planning to hit several spots in one day, especially if you're traveling as a group or family, since splitting the cost per person works out cheaper than booking app rides one-way or hiring a driver — plus you get complete freedom to stop wherever and whenever you like without waiting for transport. Both major chains and local operators offer rentals in the city, and many let you pick up and drop off at the bus terminal or airport, so you can start your trip right away. Prices start around 900-1,500 baht per day depending on car size.

What to prepare: you're legally required to have a valid driver's license (foreign visitors should carry an International Driving Permit alongside their home license), and it's worth getting full-coverage insurance. The route to Phimai is mostly a major road and an easy drive, but the way to Wang Nam Khiao and Dan Khun Thot has some hill sections and winding roads, so allow extra travel time and make sure you have enough fuel. Before taking the car, photograph and video the whole vehicle as a record of its condition, check the tires and brakes, and check parking arrangements at each stop. Overall, if your itinerary focuses on areas outside the city, renting a car is the most worthwhile choice.
blocks.tipHtml: Tip: Choose full-coverage insurance (not just the minimum), and video the whole car before you drive off, to protect yourself against damage claims when you return it. If you're visiting both Phimai and Wang Nam Khiao in one day, set off early since the combined distance is fairly long.
pros: Maximum freedom to visit Phimai, Dan Khun Thot, and Wang Nam Khiao on your own schedule
Great value when traveling with a group or visiting multiple spots outside the city
Air-conditioned, room for luggage — suits families with kids or elderly members
Pick up and drop off in town or at the station — start your trip right away
cons: Requires a valid driver's license (foreign visitors should carry an IDP) and full insurance is recommended
The route to Wang Nam Khiao and Dan Khun Thot has some hill sections and winding roads
Long distances outside the city — allow extra time and keep enough fuel

blocks.title: Which one should you choose
blocks.html: The short version, by travel style: coming from Bangkok on a budget and want to arrive fast, bus/van at about 3-4 hours is the main answer · want the scenery and aren't in a rush, the Isan rail line arriving downtown is worth trying at least once · short in-town trips on a budget, songthaews and tuk-tuks are the best value during the day · carrying heavy bags, returning late, or heading somewhere songthaews don't reach, Grab/metered taxi is more convenient · and if you're heading to Phimai Historical Park (~60 km), Dan Khun Thot, or Wang Nam Khiao, renting a car is usually the best value and most freedom, especially traveling as a group or covering several out-of-town spots in one day · flights into Nakhon Ratchasima airport are very limited, so most people choose road transport or the train instead.

faq.q: How long does it take from Bangkok to Korat, and what should I take?
faq.a: By road, buses and vans from Mo Chit 2 bus terminal take about 3-4 hours depending on traffic, running the motorway and Mittraphap Road straight into Korat. Fares run a few hundred baht per trip, with frequent departures throughout the day. The Isan rail line arrives at Nakhon Ratchasima station in the city center — scenic, but slower than the road. It suits travelers who aren't in a rush. For most people who want to arrive quickly and cheaply, the bus or van is the main choice.

faq.q: How do you get around in Korat city — is there Grab?
faq.a: In the city there are fixed-route songthaews, which are the cheapest option (tens of baht per person), tuk-tuks for short trips, metered taxis, and Grab, which works reliably in town. Grab is convenient when carrying heavy bags, returning late, or heading somewhere songthaews don't reach, since you see the price before booking. However, there are fewer cars than in Bangkok, so late at night or heading outside the city you may wait longer or struggle to find a ride. It's best to use songthaews during the day and keep Grab as a backup once they stop running.

faq.q: How do you get to Phimai Historical Park from Korat city?
faq.a: Phimai Historical Park is about 60 kilometers from the city center, and there are several ways to get there. The cheapest is a songthaew or bus service running to Phimai from town, but you'll need to allow extra time and check the schedule carefully. The most convenient and freest option is renting a car and driving yourself, or hiring a car with a driver or booking a tour, especially if you're traveling with others or want to stop at other spots along the way. Renting a car works out better value than booking a one-way app ride, since finding a return ride from Phimai is difficult.

faq.q: Do you need to rent a car to visit Korat?
faq.a: It depends on your itinerary. If you're only visiting places in the city — the Thao Suranari Monument, markets, malls, and the night market — songthaews, tuk-tuks, and Grab are enough, no rental needed. But if you're planning to visit out-of-town spots like Phimai Historical Park, Dan Khun Thot, or Wang Nam Khiao, which are far away and not well served by public transport, renting a car or hiring a driver is much better value and gives you more freedom, especially traveling as a group or family where splitting the cost per person brings it down.

Nakhon Ratchasima airport has very limited commercial flights and doesn't operate continuously like major airports, so it isn't a main option for most tourists. Most travelers coming from Bangkok choose bus/van or the Isan rail line instead, since they're more convenient, run frequently, and offer better value. If you're planning to fly, be sure to check the latest flight schedule carefully, as service can change over time.
